teach.heading: 10 more, 10 less
teach.body: Adding 10 changes only the tens digit by one. 10 more than 342 is 352. 10 less than 342 is 332. When the tens digit is 9, 10 more makes a new hundred: 10 more than 392 is 402.

teach.heading: 100 more, 100 less
teach.body: Adding 100 changes only the hundreds digit by one. 100 more than 342 is 442. 100 less than 342 is 242.

teach.heading: Skip counting
teach.body: Skip counting means counting in jumps. Counting by 10s from 240 gives 240, 250, 260, 270. Counting by 100s from 150 gives 150, 250, 350, 450. Counting backwards uses less each time.

teach.heading: Patterns on the number line
teach.body: On a number line, equal jumps are the same length. Jumps of 10 land on numbers that have the same ones digit. Jumps of 100 land on numbers with the same tens and ones digits.

guided_practice.hint: Think about 300 and 5. Taking 10 away crosses a hundred.

questions: A. Write the number that is 10 more: 427, 590, 698, 801.
B. Write the number that is 10 less: 427, 500, 610, 1000.
C. Write the number that is 100 more and 100 less: 350, 702, 900.
D. Continue each pattern with 4 more numbers: (a) 15, 25, 35 (b) 420, 520, 620 (c) 900, 850, 800.
E. A pattern starts at 210 and counts by 20s. Write the first six numbers. Which numbers have a 0 in the ones place? Why?
answers: E. 210, 230, 250, 270, 290, 310. All of them have 0 in the ones place, because adding 20 never changes the ones digit.

quiz.explain: Tens digit 9 plus one makes ten tens, so a new hundred.
Hundreds digit goes down by one.
1000 is 100 tens, and taking away one ten leaves 99 tens.
